metadata.title: Confederate Army of Northern Virginia -- Corps, Division, Brigade Level OOB
sources: Busey, John W. and Martin, David G. -- Regimental Strengths and Losses at Gettysburg (Longstreet House, 1994)
OR Vol. 27, Parts I and II
Gottfried, Bradley M. -- Brigades of Gettysburg (Da Capo Press, 2002)
Coddington, Edwin B. -- The Gettysburg Campaign (Scribner's, 1968)

commander.name: General Robert E. Lee
commander.notes: Lee was ill during the battle -- possibly a cardiac episode. His discretionary orders to Ewell on July 1 and the controversial delay of Longstreet's July 2 assault are among the most debated command decisions of the campaign.

commander.name: Lieutenant General James Longstreet
commander.notes: Longstreet strongly opposed Lee's decision to attack at Gettysburg and favored a strategic flanking movement. His delay in executing the July 2 assault remains one of the most debated controversies of the campaign.

commander.name: Lieutenant General Richard S. Ewell
commander.notes: Ewell's failure to take Cemetery Hill on July 1 evening -- despite Lee's discretionary order -- is one of the most debated moments of the battle.

commander.name: Lieutenant General Ambrose Powell Hill
commander.fate: Survived Gettysburg -- ill during the battle
commander.notes: Hill was ill during much of the battle. His corps opened the battle when Heth's division marched toward Gettysburg against Hill's instructions to avoid a general engagement.

commander.name: Major General John Bell Hood
commander.fate: Left arm permanently paralyzed July 2 -- artillery fragment

commander.name: Major General George E. Pickett
commander.notes: Pickett watched the charge from the rear and survived. His division did not. He never forgave Lee.

divisions.notes: Contains the Stonewall Brigade. Fought at Culp's Hill throughout.

commander.name: Major General Henry Heth
commander.fate: Wounded July 1 -- shot in head; folded paper in hat cushioned the blow

brigades.key_action: Rose Woods and Wheatfield -- one of the most effective Confederate brigade attacks of the battle.

commander.name: Brigadier General William Barksdale
commander.fate: KIA July 2 -- mortally wounded leading the Peach Orchard charge; died July 3

brigades.key_action: Shattered the Peach Orchard salient. Barksdale rode ahead of his men and was mortally wounded.
brigades.flag_notes: Barksdale's charge -- his being mortally wounded ahead of his men is a vignette candidate.

brigades.key_action: Rose Woods and Wheatfield. Semmes mortally wounded.
Reached the farthest Confederate penetration toward Cemetery Ridge on July 2 before Crawford drove them back.

commander.name: Brigadier General Evander Law
commander.fate: Survived -- assumed division command when Hood wounded

brigades.key_action: Attacked Big Round Top and Little Round Top. The 15th Alabama's assault on the 20th Maine is the most famous regimental combat of the battle.
Devil's Den and Triangular Field.
Wheatfield and toward Little Round Top -- one of the hardest-hit Confederate brigades of July 2.
Devil's Den and Plum Run gorge.

commander.name: Brigadier General Richard Garnett
commander.fate: KIA July 3 -- killed on horseback at The Angle; body never officially identified

brigades.key_action: Center of Pickett's charge -- reached The Angle. Garnett killed on horseback. 64.5% casualties.

commander.name: Brigadier General James Kemper
commander.fate: Severely wounded July 3 -- shot through groin; survived

brigades.key_action: Right of Pickett's line -- hit by Stannard's flanking fire. Kemper severely wounded.

commander.name: Brigadier General Lewis Armistead
commander.fate: Mortally wounded July 3 -- shot moments after breaching The Angle with his hat on his sword; died July 5
commander.notes: Armistead and Union General Hancock were close friends before the war.

brigades.key_action: Achieved the deepest Confederate penetration -- the High Water Mark of the Confederacy.
brigades.flag_notes: HIGHEST PRIORITY Confederate placement July 3: Armistead's breach of The Angle is the climactic moment of the battle.

brigades.key_action: July 2 evening -- briefly seized the crest of Cemetery Hill before being driven back.
brigades.flag_notes: Cemetery Hill assault -- brigade advances up the hill, occupies crest for 1-2 ticks, then driven back.

commander.name: Colonel Isaac Avery
commander.fate: Mortally wounded July 2 -- wrote final message in his own blood: 'Tell my father I died with my face to the enemy'

brigades.key_action: Cemetery Hill assault alongside Hays. Avery killed writing his blood-message.
brigades.flag_notes: Avery's blood-written dying message is a vignette-worthy human story.

brigades.key_action: Flank attack on Barlow's Knoll July 1 -- swept around the Union right and rolled up the XI Corps. Gordon personally gave water to the fallen Barlow. The two men met again after the war.
brigades.flag_notes: Gordon's flanking attack -- wide sweeping movement around Union right flank across multiple ticks.

brigades.key_action: Flank guard on York Road during Early's July 1 attack. Minimal engagement.
The Stonewall Brigade -- most famous in the Confederate army, formerly Jackson's own. Culp's Hill July 2-3.
Culp's Hill -- heavy fighting July 2-3.
Culp's Hill fighting July 2-3.
Contains 1st Maryland Confederate Infantry -- fighting near the 1st Maryland Union Infantry at Culp's Hill.
brigades.flag_notes: 1st Maryland Confederate vs 1st Maryland Union -- Marylanders vs Marylanders. Narrative layer flag.

brigades.key_action: Attacked south from Oak Hill along the Railroad Cut July 1. Heavy fighting all three days.
Swept across the fields north of Gettysburg July 1 -- overwhelmed the XI Corps and drove them through the town.

commander.name: Brigadier General Alfred Iverson
commander.fate: Survived -- never given another brigade command after Gettysburg

brigades.key_action: One of the most catastrophic brigade-level disasters of the Civil War. Advanced in perfect alignment directly into the stone wall ambush. ~900 men killed, wounded, or captured in minutes.
brigades.flag_notes: CRITICAL ANIMATION: brigade advances in perfect alignment, then is suddenly shot down. The contrast between the orderly advance and sudden destruction is the dramatic core.

brigades.key_action: Exploited the gap left by O'Neal's failure and Iverson's destruction on Oak Ridge.

commander.name: Colonel Edward O'Neal
commander.fate: Survived -- never promoted to brigadier general

brigades.key_action: O'Neal's attack miscarried -- he failed to lead personally, kept a regiment back without authority.
Nearly broke through Cemetery Ridge July 2 before the 1st Minnesota's sacrifice charge stopped them. Enfiladed by the 16th Vermont July 3.
brigades.flag_notes: Wilcox's July 2 advance is the specific force the 1st Minnesota charged into. Must be placed directly opposite the 1st Minnesota's attack vector.

brigades.key_action: Florida brigade -- advanced with Wilcox July 2. 52.3% casualties.
Briefly broke through Cemetery Ridge July 2 evening -- reached the crest before being driven back.
brigades.flag_notes: Wright's breakthrough -- brigade must be shown briefly reaching Cemetery Ridge crest before being repulsed.

brigades.key_action: Half-hearted skirmish-line advance July 2 -- failed to press the attack.
Not ordered forward July 2 -- sat out most of the fighting.

commander.name: Brigadier General James Pettigrew
commander.fate: Survived Gettysburg -- mortally wounded Falling Waters July 14
commander.notes: Pettigrew assumed division command; Colonel James Marshall commanded the brigade during the July 3 charge and was killed.

brigades.key_action: McPherson's Ridge July 1. Left column of July 3 assault. The 26th NC suffered the highest Confederate regimental casualties at Gettysburg.
brigades.flag_notes: 26th NC casualties must be tracked precisely -- heaviest Confederate regimental losses of the battle.

brigades.key_action: Far left of July 3 assault -- collapsed under flanking fire from the 8th Ohio.
brigades.flag_notes: Brockenbrough's collapse -- brigade breaks and retreats WHILE Pettigrew's other brigades still advance. Must show diverging movement.

commander.name: Brigadier General James Archer
commander.fate: Captured July 1 -- first Confederate general captured since Lee assumed command

brigades.key_action: Archer captured July 1. Fry led the brigade in the July 3 charge and was wounded reaching The Angle.
Railroad Cut disaster July 1. Led the brigade again in the July 3 charge suffering 52% casualties total.
brigades.flag_notes: Davis's Railroad Cut disaster -- brigade must be shown advancing into the cut, then struck from the flank by the 6th Wisconsin.

commander.name: Brigadier General James Lane
commander.fate: Survived -- assumed division command when Pender fell

brigades.key_action: Drove I Corps from Seminary Ridge July 1. July 3 charge on the right of Trimble's command.
Supported July 1 attack -- largely held in reserve July 2-3.
Delivered the decisive blow that broke the Union I Corps on Seminary Ridge July 1.
brigades.flag_notes: Perrin's breakthrough on Seminary Ridge July 1 -- must show brigade advancing through the Seminary grounds and breaking the Union line.

successor.name: Colonel William Lowrance
successor.assumed_command: July 1 -- commanded brigade for July 3 charge

brigades.key_action: Devastated on Seminary Ridge July 1 -- 66.5% casualties. Remnant advanced in the July 3 charge under Lowrance.
